Title: Medication-Related Dizziness: If It Started After a New Prescription

Description:
Falls are the leading cause of injury-related death among older adults in the US (CDC). Blood pressure medications, benzodiazepines/sleep aids, and antihistamines are especially likely to cause dizziness — and taking 5 or more medications (polypharmacy) raises the risk even further.

Rise slowly from bed or a chair for blood pressure meds, move carefully at night for sleep aids, and ask your pharmacist about non-drowsy antihistamines. If you're on 5+ medications, ask for a full medication review — and never stop a new prescription on your own if it's causing dizziness.
